Thesis:
One of the principal challenges facing the future of HPC software development is the encapsulation of architectural complexity

Sustaining software encapsulation challenges of the future
Software to punch through the Memory wall
Until processing starts to move out into the memory, the memory wall is only getting worse
Must program for deep memory hierarchies
cache-based threading, nano-tasking, blocking, memory affinity, 
Encapsulate System Factorization
Separate “curves” for nodes, interconnect, and I/O follow best-of breed trajectories and are integrated 
Heterogeneous computing
Linux nodes age like fruit flies
software must manage differing CPU speeds, memory sizes, interconnect latency/b-w, and memory
Fault tolerant software systems
interconnect, nodes, I/O
Like Blue Gene - must have self-correction to scale

Disruptive software encapsulation challenges of the future( other market drivers besides clustering )
Data-centric computing ( OLTP, Warehouses )
Getting too expensive to save, move, visualize data
Bringing services too the data
e.g. viz engines, direct attached storage devices
Software must become more data-aware
higher-level schema for data partitioning, movement, and affinity
Reconfigurable computing ( signal processing, cryptoanalysis )
Xilinx and Altera have multi-million transistor FPGAs which fit into Linux clusters
can burn in multiple FP ALUs

Disruptive software encapsulation challenges of the future ( other market drivers besides clustering )
Software integration of smarter components ( general trend of making each component in a system more capable )
how many computing devices are in your car?
Soon: Smart NICS, Smart switches, Smart disks
message processing on the NIC
network-aware gather/scatter
disk-based stride/sub-block processing
Later: Smart memory
balance of CPU and memory across architecture
breaking memory-access/FPU components of algorithms up into different instruction streams.

Software Futures
Compiler design/Run-time design
Computing across heterogeneous resources
disks, NICS,CPU, memory
Deeper and deeper memory hierarchy
High-level language to FPGA/VHDL
Explicit Data management ( remember NEWS and HPF:::Layout )
threading everywhere - even in the CPU level
enable gray area between compile and run times
e.g., run-time compilation, telescoping compilers ( Kennedy )
Language trends
Fortran into C++ - happening now
C++  into Java- happening soon ( attacking from the bottom )
Java into ??? ( more explicit language based concurrency? )

Vision Summary:
The Software Revolution must move the complexity of the evolving cluster architecture into compilers, run-time systems, encapsulating components, and perhaps languages to manage the revolution of architectural complexity that is coming down the road.
